_comment: Evaluation of each Book of Shapes pattern against the blog's components/graphics generators. verdict: covered = we already have an equivalent | port = strong fit worth building | adapt = good idea, needs rework | skip = aesthetic or technical mismatch. See EVALUATION.md.

arcs_1: Rotation by whole turns is a free seamless loop. No arc generator exists.
backpack-grid: Rounded rectangles contradict the zero-border-radius rule.
brockmann_arcs: 2 KB — the lightest of all 57. Quantised angles suit the grid aesthetic.
chaos_circles: Hand-drawn wobble reads as sketch, not brutalist hard edge.
chevron_blocks: Ruled hexagons with sparse solid fills — lattice.ts already does hex.
concentric_arc_truchet_2: Truchet tiling: per-cell rotation, lattice.ts hosts it, rotation loops.
concentric_arc_truchet_3: Mirrored variant of the above; build one Truchet, parameterise the tile.
concentric_noise_rings: Radial contour — same idea as contour, different coordinate system.
deformed_grid_mesh: Noise-displaced grid; 1.3 MB as drawn. Needs our density control.
deformed_grid_mesh_2: Parameter variant of the above, not a distinct idea.
dna_helix: Illustrative subject, not a background. Occlusion-heavy.
flow_dots: Dot grid coming apart into strands — a motion idea dot-grid lacks.
flow_lines: Built: integrating streamlines breaks the smoothness invariant. Ship the direction field instead.
flow_poles: Same advection trap as flow_lines; the orbiting poles are still worth having.
halftone_sphere: Depicts a sphere. Subject matter, not texture.
hiding-squares: Mask-per-cell reveal; scatter-blocks covers the look, not the masking.
iso_test_noise_field: Isometric height-field landscape. Needs the occlusion colour first.
isometric-cube-grid: Shipped as iso-cubes (blog#138), once occlusion existed.
isometric_ribbon_grid: Noise-driven parallelogram cells over a triangular lattice.
jittery_squares_grid: Order-to-chaos gradient across the frame — scatter-blocks is uniform.
joy_division_mesh: Wireframe mesh version of ridgeline — a genuinely different surface.
line_based_circles: Circles as loose segments — deconstruction suits the brutalist edge.
lissajous_field: Parametric curves; integer frequency ratios close the loop by construction.
masked_letter_grid: Needs font metrics; not portable to a pure-string generator.
modular_circle: 24 KB. Concentric modular rings — we have no radial generator at all.
nested_polygons: Inscribed polygons; rotation per ring animates on whole turns.
nested_polygons_filled: 694 KB as drawn; the noise-masked fill is the reusable half.
noise_circle_1: Organic blob edge; clashes with hard-edged geometry.
noise_landscape_1: contour and ridgeline between them cover this.
phyllotaxis-bloom: Golden angle; sample once, project a whole-turn rotation.
polar_mesh: Polar-coordinate mesh — the radial counterpart to our grid lattices.
radial_harmony: 35 KB. Concentric circles with radial divisions — clean and light.
radial_spokes: Shipped as radial-spokes (blog#138) — closed the radial gap.
rect_field_void: Negative space as the composition. Strongly brutalist.
resonance_field: Multi-source interference, 1 MB as drawn. Cap the source count.
ripple_grid: Concentric wave distortion of a grid; sources can orbit on whole cycles.
rose_mesh: Rose curves; pretty but reads decorative rather than structural.
scattered-cube-grid: 969 KB, and the scatter re-rolls badly under density.
signal_decay: Decaying oscillation — reads as terminal/signal, matches the site voice.
sine-cube: Isometric cubes on a sine field; occlusion prerequisite.
spiral_dot_field: 50 KB. Spiral dot arrangement; rotation loops cleanly.
spiral_mesh: Spiral trajectories as a mesh; 438 KB as drawn.
spiral_morph: Grid warped toward an Archimedean spiral — the warp is the reusable idea.
triangular_mosaic: triangle-grid (PR #132) covers the tiling; the order-to-chaos ramp does not.
wave-field: Shipped as flow-field (blog#138) — the advection-free form of flow_lines.
wavy_fabric: Interwoven wave lines — over/under weaving is a real occlusion use outside iso.
wavy_lines_converging: Five interweaving sines; close to contour with a convergence envelope.
